economic_assumptions.note: Safety margin confirmed by owner 16 October. Other stated values retained from prior report; not read from live configuration. Thresholds do not themselves qualify thermal supply.

notes: All dense cells are mathematical estimates, not new measurements.
The surface pools actual inlet conditions from four runs. Its outdoor-temperature pattern does not isolate a causal weather effect.

Actual inlet range approximately 12.7–25.2C and changed metering method are retained in point provenance. Inlet-reference matrix is a descriptive interpolation, not a selectable independent condition.
Whole-run holdout errors are diagnostics from four runs, not confidence intervals. Exact interpolation is zero training error by construction.
Extrapolation outside the accepted (outside,power) convex hull is explicitly flagged, even within the 5–16C and 30–100% rectangular grid.
Full-period heat uses nameplate-based 2000m3/h airflow. Installed airflow and meter systematic uncertainty are not included in fit errors.
Dedicated circuit excludes equipment outside that meter; historical house-baseline increments retain their own scope.
Defrost-like/transient points are displayed but excluded from the normal-heating interpolation. No complete-cycle defrost or seasonal COP model.
Reference grid for the bundled opt-in runtime surface; live settings and automatic/manual selection remain separately controlled.

model.status: Bundled opt-in runtime v2 surface; measured-point mode remains default
model.method: Minimum-curvature thin-plate radial-basis interpolation with affine trend; zero smoothing; equal point weights.
model.formula: q=(Tout-10.5)/5.5, r=(power-65)/35; F(q,r)=sum(w_i*d_i^2*ln(d_i))+a0+a1*q+a2*r; phi(0)=0. Interpolate full-period air rise, electrical kW and descriptive inlet C. Heat kW=0.67*airRise; COP=heat/electrical kW.
model.coefficient_order: first n rows radial weights at normalized centers; final 3 rows constant, normalized outside, normalized power; columns airRiseC, electricKW, descriptiveInletC
